texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Precipitation accumulations were variable across agro-Manitoba over the past seven days. Isolated rain and snow resulted in accumulations varying from 0 mm to 43.9 mm. Reston received the most precipitation with 43.9 mm (Table 1).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Soil moisture conditions are good in the Northwest and Interlake areas where snow was more plentiful this winter. Soil moisture levels are a concern in Eastern and Southern regions of the province where modest snow cover over the winter months contributed to lower spring run-off levels. Accordingly, dugouts may not be fully re-charged in these areas.
texts.text: Soil moisture conditions are good in the Northwest and Interlake areas where snow was more plentiful this winter. Soil moisture levels are a concern in Eastern and Southern regions of the province where modest snow cover over the winter months contributed to lower spring run-off levels. Accordingly, dugouts may not be fully re-charged in these areas.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Livestock
texts.text: Livestock

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Producers have begun checking and fixing fences on their pastures and monitoring water levels on dugouts prior to cattle turnout which won't be until later in May.
texts.text: Producers have begun checking and fixing fences on their pastures and monitoring water levels on dugouts prior to cattle turnout which won't be until later in May.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Most cattle remain in their winter-feeding areas. Some operations have moved livestock to smaller paddocks adjacent to corrals to allow animals access to drier and cleaner areas with more space. Majority of operations are calving (with some wrapping up and others just beginning).
texts.text: Most cattle remain in their winter-feeding areas. Some operations have moved livestock to smaller paddocks adjacent to corrals to allow animals access to drier and cleaner areas with more space. Majority of operations are calving (with some wrapping up and others just beginning).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Hay supplies are generally adequate with some producers expecting carry-over. Hay is still available for sale for producers who may need to top up their feed supplies. Several operations are supplementing cattle with grain or other higher energy feed to boost energy levels in the ration during lactation.
texts.text: Hay supplies are generally adequate with some producers expecting carry-over. Hay is still available for sale for producers who may need to top up their feed supplies. Several operations are supplementing cattle with grain or other higher energy feed to boost energy levels in the ration during lactation.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Fall rye and winter wheat fields survived the winter in good condition. However, their growth is slow due to cooler temperatures.
texts.text: Fall rye and winter wheat fields survived the winter in good condition. However, their growth is slow due to cooler temperatures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Fertilization of hay fields via manure application and commercial fertilizer has begun.
texts.text: Fertilization of hay fields via manure application and commercial fertilizer has begun.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · A handful of dairy operations have begun seeding forages in the eastern part of the province over the weekend. However, rainy weather conditions have stalled any further field work.
texts.text: A handful of dairy operations have begun seeding forages in the eastern part of the province over the weekend. However, rainy weather conditions have stalled any further field work.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Regional Comments
texts.text: Regional Comments

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Moisture received in the past seven days was quickly absorbed into the soil without significant run-off. Modest flows were observed in the Pipestone Creek, and the Souris River is experiencing average flows.
texts.text: Moisture received in the past seven days was quickly absorbed into the soil without significant run-off. Modest flows were observed in the Pipestone Creek, and the Souris River is experiencing average flows.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Seeding has started west of Brandon and near Rapid City, however low-lying areas are still quite wet. Some prebanding may take place this week, and sprayers are being prepped for burn-off application.
texts.text: Seeding has started west of Brandon and near Rapid City, however low-lying areas are still quite wet. Some prebanding may take place this week, and sprayers are being prepped for burn-off application.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter cereal survival may be spotty, as there are only a few fields in the area. Topdressing is likely to occur anytime now through the end of next month for winter cereals.
texts.text: Winter cereal survival may be spotty, as there are only a few fields in the area. Topdressing is likely to occur anytime now through the end of next month for winter cereals.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field conditions remain saturated in the Roblin and Dauphin area as they received precipitation mid-week. Conditions have improved in the Swan Valley region. Field prep operations have begun, and there has been a small amount of spring wheat seeding in the Swan Valley area. Drier conditions are needed this week for other areas to begin seeding.
texts.text: Field conditions remain saturated in the Roblin and Dauphin area as they received precipitation mid-week. Conditions have improved in the Swan Valley region. Field prep operations have begun, and there has been a small amount of spring wheat seeding in the Swan Valley area. Drier conditions are needed this week for other areas to begin seeding.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fall rye and winter cereals are in good condition.
texts.text: Fall rye and winter cereals are in good condition.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Central
texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rainfall this week halted most seeding and field operations across the province. The rains largely infiltrated the soil with minimal runoff providing necessary moisture for cash crop establishment and pasture growth.
texts.text: Rainfall this week halted most seeding and field operations across the province. The rains largely infiltrated the soil with minimal runoff providing necessary moisture for cash crop establishment and pasture growth.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Limited seeding has occurred, with a small number of spring wheat and pea acres being seeded, particularly in lighter soil regions. Some liquid fertilizer and manure applications have also taken place.
texts.text: Limited seeding has occurred, with a small number of spring wheat and pea acres being seeded, particularly in lighter soil regions. Some liquid fertilizer and manure applications have also taken place.

texts.orig: S
texts.text: S

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Producers are actively preparing seeding and other field equipment to move quickly once conditions improve. Weed emergence has begun, including volunteer canola and flixweed.
texts.text: Manitoba Producers are actively preparing seeding and other field equipment to move quickly once conditions improve. Weed emergence has begun, including volunteer canola and flixweed.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Eastern
texts.text: Eastern

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Limited seeding has occurred in the region. A few fields of wheat and some pea acres are in the ground. Limited manure applications have begun on drier fields. Producers have been busy getting their seeding equipment ready so they can plant as soon as conditions allow. Reports of some early liquid fertilizer (28-0-0) applications have also been received.
texts.text: Limited seeding has occurred in the region. A few fields of wheat and some pea acres are in the ground. Limited manure applications have begun on drier fields. Producers have been busy getting their seeding equipment ready so they can plant as soon as conditions allow. Reports of some early liquid fertilizer (28-0-0) applications have also been received.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter cereal fertilizer applications are nearing completion in the region. Cropping plans are being shifted slightly this year as a function of profitability. Canola acres are projected to be down while corn and wheat acres will increase. For some farms this year sunflowers will make a return to the rotation.
texts.text: Winter cereal fertilizer applications are nearing completion in the region. Cropping plans are being shifted slightly this year as a function of profitability. Canola acres are projected to be down while corn and wheat acres will increase. For some farms this year sunflowers will make a return to the rotation.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Interlake
texts.text: Interlake

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A small amount of seeding has begun in the Interlake due to moist soil conditions and intermittent rainfall over the past week. The crops that are being seeded include spring wheat, oats, and some peas.
texts.text: A small amount of seeding has begun in the Interlake due to moist soil conditions and intermittent rainfall over the past week. The crops that are being seeded include spring wheat, oats, and some peas.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fall rye and winter wheat are in good condition with no concerns to report. Fall rye has started to green up with no visible winterkill so far.
texts.text: Fall rye and winter wheat are in good condition with no concerns to report. Fall rye has started to green up with no visible winterkill so far.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Very limited field operations, including fertilization and tillage, are ongoing in the Interlake region. Grass seed is being broadcast in certain areas. Fall rye urea fertilizer will begin in the coming days. Fertilization is underway in Timothy established seed fields in some parts of the region.
texts.text: Very limited field operations, including fertilization and tillage, are ongoing in the Interlake region. Grass seed is being broadcast in certain areas. Fall rye urea fertilizer will begin in the coming days. Fertilization is underway in Timothy established seed fields in some parts of the region.
